storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form declared by each id_kind row.

Storage implementations MAY store producer-allocated raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ak:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The payload construction MUST be fixed by that kind's id_form and identity_authority columns, never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses UUIDv7; event_derived uses the creating Event's 33-byte token; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest-suite code followed by the complete 32-byte digest under its registered kind-specific preimage contract. v1 Event and suite-tagged identities accept only registered active suite codes with high nibble 0x0; this constraint does not give that nibble any meaning beyond the suite code. A UUID version nibble or digest-suite byte alone never proves identity authority.

A producer_allocated UUIDv7 is never a globally sufficient protocol identity. Its canonical identity key is (mint_authority, typed_id), where mint_authority is the DID whose accepted proof authorized the first durable appearance of that ID. Bare typed-ID lookup, cross-authority deduplication, and last-writer-wins collision repair are forbidden.

Storage implementations MAY store producer_allocated UUID values as raw 16-byte UUIDs. Event-derived and suite-tagged full-digest IDs MUST instead store their raw 33-byte token; they MUST NOT use a native UUID column.

The id_form is fixed by registry kind and never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses RFC 9562 UUIDv7; event_derived uses the same canonical 33-byte token as its creating Event ID; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest suite code followed by all 32 digest octets. Both token forms serialize as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters.

A database MAY intern any full Realm wire identity in a canonical Realm table and use a database-local surrogate pk for joins, indexes, and foreign keys. That pk is never serialized or signed. The canonical table MUST retain a unique lossless 33-byte Realm identity (or its full typed wire form), and every realm_pk foreign key MUST resolve to the same wire Realm identity carried by the protocol record.

Every special_forms row declares payload_pattern, the machine-readable value space of everything after its ak:<kind>: prefix; wire_form remains the human-readable template and payload_pattern is its only normative expansion. A schema, OpenAPI or profile carrier MAY be narrower than payload_pattern for a specific field, but MUST NOT accept an octet payload_pattern rejects, and MUST end-anchor so no trailing byte escapes the declared value space.

producer_allocated_identity_contract.security_rationale: UUIDv7 randomness and timestamp layout do not authenticate the allocator. Binding every producer-selected ID to the accepted genesis signer prevents an attacker from claiming another producer's ID by copying or predicting the UUID.

issuer_record_identity_contract.v1_suite_code_constraint: The complete uint8 suite wire code is encoded unchanged, but v1 accepts only registered active codes whose high nibble is 0x0; this is not a Realm derivation-class nibble.

closed_encoding.audience: canonical_bare_resource_service_did; never an HTTP origin or endpoint URL
closed_encoding.credential_binding: credential_class is standard or recovery_session; holder_binding is required; device_binding is required only for standard human_device and forbidden for recovery_candidate_device and agent_runtime

issuer_record_identity_contract.signed_claim_binding: Every preimage field except fixed schema is a signed JWT claim, including credential_class and holder_binding; kind is the fixed credential kind and jti is the derived typed ID. Verifiers MUST reconstruct the complete preimage from signed claims and recompute jti, so different credential classes or holder bindings cannot share one valid ID.
issuer_record_identity_contract.session_chain_rule: session_id is independently allocated before first issuance, refresh inherits it, and it MUST NOT equal or derive from grant_id
issuer_record_identity_contract.device_id_rule: No independent top-level device_id claim enters the preimage; standard human holder_binding and its complete device_binding carry accepted-device authority. Recovery candidate-device and Agent runtime holder bindings carry their own device_id and forbid device_binding.

lifecycle.refresh: one issuer transaction creates active successor and supersedes predecessor with successor_session_grant_id

account_status_record_identity_contract.digest_input: SHA-256(JCS(record fields excluding account_status_record_id and proof))
account_status_record_identity_contract.sequence_rule: status_seq starts at 1; seq=1 is active and has no previous_account_status_record_id; every successor is current+1 and names the exact current account_status_record_id

realm_token_layout.event_derived_retype_compatibility: Realm and Event token headers are identical, so an ak.realm.create Event token is byte-identical to its Realm token and retyping only swaps the ak:event: / ak:realm: prefix. v1 Realm identity is fixed to SHA-256, so only a creating Event with header 0x01 is Realm-eligible.
realm_token_layout.high_nibble_carries_no_category: The high nibble is reserved zero and carries no category information. Realm purpose lives in the signed create payload; implementations MUST NOT infer purpose from realm_id.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference using an active digest-suite id (v1: sha256 or profile-gated blake3); distinct from ak:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7. payload_pattern is the core-registered outer value space the profile MUST stay inside; the profile MAY narrow it further but MUST NOT accept an octet outside it.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Profile-scoped pseudonymous reference. Each consuming profile defines its own scope boundary and narrows the core-registered outer payload_pattern; it MUST NOT accept an octet outside that space. E2EE credential pseudonyms are Realm-scoped, while push pseudonyms are scoped to the registered recipient service, principal, device, route and salt epoch. Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque install-plan token; do not parse it as UUIDv7.
special_forms.description: Applet install-plan identifier. The suffix is an opaque non-empty base64url token.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte receipt-claims digest or the complete typed content-addressed identifier.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed ServiceRegistrationReceipt identifier derived from canonical receipt claims. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt claims)).

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32 raw challenge octets together with the challenge consumption ledger row; it is registry-local single-use state, never a federated object ID and never a native UUID column.
special_forms.description: Single-use Organization registration control challenge identifier issued by ak.root.identity.organization_registration.command.prepare. It is registry-allocated, neither content-addressed nor Event-derived, and it never denotes a durable protocol object.

allocation.payload_encoding: 32 octets rendered as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
allocation.uniqueness_rule: The registry MUST atomically reserve the value before returning it and MUST reallocate on any collision with a live or consumed ledger row; a challenge value is never reissued.
allocation.consumption_rule: The registry MUST consume the challenge inside the same transaction that persists (challenge_id, canonical_request_digest, outcome).
allocation.replay_rule: Only a byte-identical retry may return the recorded outcome; the same challenge_id carrying any different canonical_request_digest, or a consumed challenge_id with no matching successful ledger row, MUST be rejected with organization_registration_challenge_invalid.
allocation.security_rationale: A caller-chosen or request-derived challenge would let the caller pick freshness and defeat single-use consumption, so the registry mints the full 256-bit value itself and binds the outcome to the exact canonical request bytes.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte receipt-claims digest or the complete typed content-addressed identifier.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed OrganizationRegistrationReceipt identifier. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt_claims)), where receipt_claims is exactly the receipt object with registration_receipt_id and proof both omitted; it is the same content-addressed family as service_registration_receipt and MUST NOT be reused as a Realm capability, membership, notary designation or service delegation.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte delegation digest or the complete typed content-addressed reference.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed membership-compensation delegation reference. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal the SHA-256 delegation_digest derived from the profile-defined digest-free canonical core.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as a content-addressed canonical Seal hash.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed Seal identifier using an active digest-suite id (v1: sha256 or profile-gated blake3), the same suite-tagged shape as ak:blob:<digest-suite>:<digest>. The suite segment is not fixed to sha256: a Seal id is a critical field, so its suite prefix MUST equal the Realm digest_algorithm and MUST be an active row of registry/digest-suite-registry.json; any other prefix fails closed with unsupported_digest_algorithm. See spec/v1/zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 6.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.
special_forms.description: Canonical protocol cell identifier. The complete ak.component.<facet-path>.v<n> family identifier is embedded unchanged after ak:cell:. When the registry declares cell_subject: null for a family, the canonical subject segment is the literal ASCII string 'null' (ak:cell:<component>:null); the cell is located by the Event envelope realm_id and implementations MUST NOT encode realm_id, Realm role classification, or any payload-derived value into that segment. See spec/v1/zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete canonical value for equality and indexing; generic consumers MUST NOT split or normalize the adapter-defined core segment.
special_forms.description: Stable DID-derived principal, actor or service identity core. It is not a DID, is not directly resolvable, and MUST be projected only by a registered DID method adapter from a canonical bare full_id. Registered as a special form rather than an id_form because its identity authority is the external DID method, not an Arkret producer or Event digest.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete canonical ak:trust_domain:<scope> value by default. A compressed schema may store the raw scope only in an explicitly named trust_domain_scope column and MUST restore the typed prefix at the persistence boundary.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk root, recovery and authorization proofs. NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete typed content-addressed identifier together with the exact canonical signer-evidence bytes.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed authenticated signer-resolution evidence reference. The suffix is the SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical evidence object under its registered digest rule.

id_kinds.description: Actor profile object ID
Moderation appeal ID derived from ak.moderation.appeal.submit and referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.
Applet registration/service ID
Audit Applet Binding ID derived from ak.audit.applet_binding.create and referenced by binding state and audit session events.
Audit release session ID derived from ak.audit.session.request. Threads request, authorize, notice, release, and close events for one bounded historical audit window.
Audit release manifest ID derived from ak.audit.release for a sealed historical release under an active audit binding/session.
Encrypted backup object ID

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_kind). A pair MAY have multiple series during rotation or migration; the active series is selected by the signed active-series record, not by server return order. Used by ak.schema.key_backup.v1.series_id and recovery strands to detect rollback. See identity/key-management.md §7.6.
Discovery/private-contact batch ID
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form
Actor-private blocklist entry ID
Call/session ID derived from the accepted ak.call.create genesis Event.

SFU-local participant handle. Scope limited to `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`; derived from `(realm_id, call_id, focus_id, device_id, issuer_service_id, ice_bucket(issued_at))` by the media service token issuer, where v1 ice_bucket is the fixed 300-second UTC bucket. MUST NOT carry any actor-identifying material; only appears in an `ak.call.state.roster_delta` join participant value and in `participant_binding`. The wire value MUST use the canonical UUIDv7-shaped `ak:rtc_participant:<uuid>` form; implementations MAY derive the random bits from the media-service token input, but the version and variant nibbles MUST satisfy the UUIDv7 pattern.
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use ak:grant:<44-char-event-token>.

Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. See zh/models/circle.md.
Agent Sidecar object ID — controller-owned private AI workspace, singleton per (realm_id, controller_id), with derived eligible-Agent access. See zh/models/sidecar.md.
Consent grant/revoke/request identifier shared by Arkret consent events and MIMI interop DTOs.
Strand object ID
Snapshot/blob chunk ID
Claim or attestation ID

Device identifier (ak:device:<uuid>). A device is a typed ID scoped to an owning principal, NOT a DID and NOT an actor principal. Device keys are registered as verification methods under the owning principal DID via ak.device.authorize.
To-device message queue ID
Event Envelope ID
Moderation/filter rule ID
Non-HTTP stream frame ID
Message franking proof ID
Durable signed capability Grant ID derived from the accepted ak.capability.grant genesis Event; distinct from short-lived SessionGrant credentials.

Short-lived signed SessionGrant credential ID derived from the Account Authority's closed immutable issuance record. JWT jti carries this typed ID; it is neither an Event ID nor an ak:grant capability ID.
Immutable Account Authority issuer-ledger lifecycle record identity derived from the complete closed unsigned record core.
Invite object ID derived from either directed ak.invite.create or third-party ak.invite.third_party genesis.

Non-secret Principal Server administrative ID for one account-owned online invite locator. The ID is exposed only on the authenticated self management surface and is distinct from the opaque bearer locator_token.
DID/key log event ID
Message object ID
Transient Signal Message preview stream instance ID; never a durable object or Event identity
Morph object ID
Notification projection ID

Identifier for a durable or reserved multi-phase protocol operation instance. It is allocated at reservation time, before the operation's first Event exists, so it can carry no content binding and MUST NOT be parsed for internal semantics; that is what id_form=producer_allocated means here, not a free-form value space.
Actor-private read cursor ID
Policy object ID
Presentation/proof exchange ID
Receipt object ID
Basis-bound AuthorizationLease identifier.
Producer-allocated Organization Recovery Key registration identity, frozen across its authorized rotation lineage.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery strand. Referenced by ak.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by RecoveryTransaction proofs. See identity/security-transactions.md §2 and crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.
Attestation object ID (e.g. ak.attestation.range_completeness).
Relation object ID
Moderation report ID derived from the accepted ak.self.moderation.report Event.
Moderation queue item ID derived as a second, distinct typed output of the accepted ak.self.moderation.report Event.
Request/correlation ID
Service-local planned route handover chain ID. The target service allocates it once and reuses it across scheduled updates and cancellation revisions for the same handover.
Snapshot manifest ID

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Directory notification subscription identifier.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_access, MLS group binding, and federation policy.
id_kinds.id_form_note: All Realm IDs are 33-byte Event tokens (encoding.md section 4.1): reserved-zero high nibble, uint4 digest suite, then all 32 digest octets, encoded as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters. The token is byte-identical to its ak.realm.create Event token; retyping only swaps the typed prefix.

id_kinds.description: Durable RecoveryTransaction, SecurityRotationTransaction, federation, or applet transaction identifier.
View object ID
Producer-allocated identity of a principal-private scheduled-send plan. It is not an Event or Message identity and MUST NOT be retyped into either one.
Producer-allocated immutable scope-private history-key request identity.
Producer-allocated immutable history-key response record identity.

uuid_form_rules: The construction is declared per kind by id_form. producer_allocated = RFC 9562 UUIDv7. event_derived = the creating Event's 33-byte token (zero reserved high nibble plus uint4 suite wire_code followed by all 32 octets of its digest), canonically encoded as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters and retyped only by replacing the ak:<kind>: prefix. The token requires strict decode plus canonical re-encode validation; regex alone is insufficient.
